body: Please share the code of you custom handlers. In general it seems like you do something bad in your handler. Also it seems like you use a very old version of netty. Please upgrade to latest 4.1 release.
@Underbalanced awesome... will have a look later today.

@normanmaurer

 I edited. Just added this...

•The exception is still thrown when I add  sslHandler.close();  before  ch.pipeline().remove(SSL_HANDLER);  in the Handshake Future Listener

•A better question might be what is the proper way to upon SSL handshake completion breakdown the SSL and remove the handlers and ensure the channels are ready for communications again?

Is there a guide so I can help debug better stuff deeper in Netty API and provide my own discovery of issues like this?
@Underbalanced this was a bug fixed by https://github.com/netty/netty/pull/5880. That said I am not sure why you would remove the SslHandler after the handshake.

@normanmaurer I was watching you fix and discuss this and I reviewed the bug on source code. I use the handshake with client authentication required as a way for my company proxies to connect to each other. The main connection stays encrypted (administrative connection), but the other bulk data like file sending and specific messages go over a second non encrypted connection. Initially it starts out encrypted as my way of authenticating the connection and exchanging connection data to confirm the new connections legitimacy and tying it to a existing session, each proxy has its own private key the SSL is broken down once the connection is good for those bulk data I do not need secured. I was designing a inner connected Proxy system to help mitigate DDOS/DOS and thus proxies talk to each other and replicate resources for the Massively Multiplayer game. I also host a revocation list for the server sides to tap into incase one of my servers becomes comprised I revoke its cert. <3 Netty 4 Life!

issue.title: SSL Handshake failure closes connection disallowing a response

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
It appears that the resolution to #5860 / #5880 in release 4.0.42 changed how a ssl handshake failure behaves. Previously, the SslHandler would call fireExceptionCaught() before setHandshakeFailure(). The order of the execution of these calls was reversed in one of these issues.

I was using the fireExceptionCaught() to send an HTTP redirect response back to the caller. Is there any way to do this in Netty 4.0.42+ ? Thanks!
